Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI, have killed several Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists, including high-profile leaders, after repelling a major attack on their positions in Kukawa, Borno State. According to a statement issued on Sunday by the Acting Media Information Officer of the Headquarters Joint Task Force (North East), Captain Mohammed Goni on X, the engagement took place on October 31 2026. “Combined troops deployed in Kukawa defeated a large-scale ISWAP assault using both ground forces and air support from the operation’s air component. “Among those neutralised were Abu Hajara, described as a high-profile member of ISWAP’s Shura Council; Abul Walid, a prominent commander and close associate of Ba Shuwa, the overall Wali of ISWAP; and two high-ranking Arab fighters. Several other terrorists were also killed in the fighting,” the post read. Following the clash, troops recovered scores of arms, ammunition and communication devices. Those killed in the earlier operation included key commanders identified as Ali Mandara Abba Gajiri (also known as Munzir), Habu Ikkima Nakif Yana Faruk and Commander Gogore. The Theatre Command said the successful defence demonstrated the combat readiness, vigilance and superior firepower of Operation HADIN KAI troops. It reaffirmed its commitment to protecting law-abiding citizens and sustaining operations aimed at the total annihilation of terrorists and the destruction of their camps in the region. The killing of senior Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) commanders in Kukawa, Borno State, comes amid an intensified military campaign against insurgent groups operating in Nigeria’s North-East, particularly around the Lake Chad Basin.
